name: Fermented cod liver oil / butter oil (Weston A. Price)

image.caption: Arrived home last night after a week away on conference to find these waiting for me...fermented cod liver oil and freeze dried adrenal glandulars...an odd welcome home present to get excited about! #paf #paleo

lead: This is a supplement pairing promoted by followers of dentist Weston A. Price, combining fermented cod liver oil with high-vitamin butter oil. Followers take it for strong teeth, bone and the facial structure they associate with them.

Followers describe the oils as supplying vitamins A and D and related fat-soluble nutrients thought to support teeth and bone. The idea comes from Price's 1939 work on traditional diets, which drew both praise and criticism from reviewers; clinical studies of this specific pairing were not found.

paras: People take the two together as a daily liquid or capsule routine, usually as part of a traditional-foods diet with raw dairy, organ meats and bone broths. Users describe it as a long-term habit rather than a short course.

Cod liver oil is a concentrated source of preformed vitamin A, for which the US upper intake for adults is 3,000 micrograms per day. Excess vitamin A can cause nausea, bone pain and liver damage. No studies of this specific pairing were found.

chain: Claimed support for bone and teeth
angle.text: Followers of the Weston A. Price Foundation take this pairing as a source of vitamins A, D and K2, aiming for stronger teeth, bone and facial structure. The link to facial structure is Price's theory from his traditional-diet surveys; clinical studies of the pairing were not found.

lead: Fermented cod liver oil combined with high-vitamin butter oil is a supplement pairing associated with the Weston A. Price Foundation, a nutrition advocacy group co-founded in 1999 by Sally Fallon and Mary G. Enig to promote the research of Canadian dentist Weston A. Price (1870 to 1948).[1] Followers use it as a source of fat-soluble vitamins, aiming for dental, skeletal and facial-structure benefits.

Price's 1939 book Nutrition and Physical Degeneration described his travels studying traditional diets and argued that processed foods caused deficiencies and disease.[1] Reviewers at the time and since have disagreed about his work: a 1940 Journal of the American Medical Association review called his approach evangelistic rather than scientific, while a Canadian Medical Association Journal review praised it.[1] The sources reviewed contain no clinical studies of the fermented cod liver oil and butter oil combination.

paras: Weston Andrew Valleau Price was a Canadian dentist, born in 1870, who graduated from the University of Michigan dental college in 1893 and practiced in Cleveland, Ohio.[1] He chaired the National Dental Association from 1914 to 1928.[1] In Nutrition and Physical Degeneration (1939) he reported on diets of communities in places including the Swiss Lötschental and among Native American, Polynesian and Aboriginal groups, claiming Western diseases such as dental decay were rare among them and that food processing removed vitamins and minerals.[1]

The Weston A. Price Foundation was co-founded in 1999 by Sally Fallon and Mary G. Enig to disseminate Price's work.[1] A separate body, the Price-Pottenger Nutrition Foundation, was established in 1952 and holds an archive of his materials.[1] The Wikipedia article on Price does not discuss butter oil or cod liver oil specifically.

In the 1920s and 1930s Price also supported the focal infection theory, which led to many tooth extractions; researchers questioned his methods by the 1930s and the theory moved to the margins of dentistry by the 1950s.[1] A 1981 critique by William T. Jarvis in Nutrition Today argued Price's work reflected a 'myth of the healthy savage' and overlooked alternative explanations such as malnutrition.[1] The Weston A. Price Foundation has published a rebuttal to critics.[1]
No studies found of fermented cod liver oil combined with high-vitamin butter oil. Studies of ordinary cod liver oil are covered in the separate cod liver oil article.

lore.intro: Within Weston Price-aligned diet communities the pairing is described as a way to obtain vitamins A, D and K-type factors from traditional foods.[1]

claims.claim: Traditional diets rich in animal fats protect teeth and facial structure.
